answer: Each identity must hold one state-registered apiary: a named site with numbered hives, inspected twice a year. One apiary backs exactly one identity; a second claim on the same hives is rejected. A gale check proves the hives are tended, not paper entries. Earning it costs 700 units in hives, bees and fees plus 120 days of tending before the first dawn inspection passes; 100 fakes cost 70,000 units and 12,000 days. The cheapest cheat is renting an apiary: the lender's own anchor freezes while its hives serve another, and a forged log fails the quartz-tagged hive seal check, exposing both.
